//: Defaults. To change anything, copy the key into config.local.json beside this file — that one is git-ignored and wins, so your settings survive a `git pull`. See config.local.example.json.
//profiles: One profile = one Claude account = one pet. Most people need exactly this one. `match` is how the hook tells accounts apart: it walks the process tree to the Electron root and reads its --user-data-dir. The profile with match=null is the fallback, and its id must stay `account1` — that is the hook's built-in default, and renaming it means the hook writes state nobody reads.

strip.//: The walking area above the dock. Anchored bottom-left of every display.

behavior.//: nagDelayMs: how long a permission prompt sits unanswered before a system notification fires. Set to 0 to notify instantly, or -1 to never notify (bubble only). It is counted from the moment the prompt is *detected*, i.e. promptSuspectMs after it actually appeared.
behavior.//promptSuspectMs: A PreToolUse with no PostToolUse behind it for this long means Claude is sitting on a permission prompt. The Notification hook does not fire for prompts in the desktop app, so this gap is the signal. Applies only to tools that always finish instantly (FAST_TOOLS in src/state.js). Bash is exempted while its shell is still alive.
behavior.//slowToolSuspectMs: Same idea, for tools that legitimately run long: Task (subagents), WebFetch, WebSearch and every mcp__* server call. There is no way to tell one of those working from one waiting, so they get a long fuse instead of a 4s one. Lower it for faster alerts and more false ones.
behavior.//inferredMaxMs: Give up on an *inferred* prompt this old. A tool call left dangling this long is usually wreckage — an interrupted turn or a killed session — not a prompt anyone will answer.
behavior.//maxNags: Notifications per prompt before Clawd shuts up about it. The bubble stays.
behavior.//notifyOnDone: Announce a turn that finished, if it ran for at least doneMinWorkMs. Set false to turn it off.
behavior.//fps: Animation rate. Lower = less CPU, choppier crab. 15/5 measured ~5% of a core for a visible working pet; 10/4 is noticeably cheaper and still reads fine.
